parsed.process: Traditional earth-mound kiln pyrolysis monitored by smoke-color changes
parsed.process_problem: Charcoal makers run 24/7 smoke-watching because the internal kiln temperature field is unobservable from only a few surface points, and earth-mound kilns lose 70-80% of the wood's energy with ~15-25% yield
parsed.recent_technique: Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) for sparse-sensor field reconstruction (RecFNO / neuraloperator)
parsed.how_it_improves: Inputs: 5-10 cheap thermocouples (or sheathed K-type probes) inserted at the base vents, mid-mound, and near the central chimney, plus one or two surface IR readings. Model: an FNO trained on simulated kiln pyrolysis physics (or a handful of instrumented kilns) maps those sparse point readings to the full continuous 3D internal temperature/heat field at each timestep, with resolution-invariant zero-shot super-resolution between sensors. Actionable output: a live reconstructed thermal map that flags the carbonization front, hot/cold pockets, and the moment the wood-charge has reached pyrolysis completion -- replacing subjective smoke-color reading with a quantitative stage indicator and a vent/air control signal. Gain: operators close vents and harvest at the true endpoint instead of over-burning, recovering several percentage points of yield and eliminating much of the 24/7 manual smoke watch.
parsed.why_recent_technique_beats_mature_approa: The mature route to a field is either dense instrumentation (you cannot pack a buried earth mound with hundreds of probes, and you certainly cannot image its interior) or classical CNN/POD reconstruction, both of which need a dense, per-kiln labeled training grid that this artisanal process never produces. FNO's new capability is reconstructing a full continuous field from only 5-10 sparse points with zero-shot super-resolution and resolution invariance -- it interpolates physically between the few probes you can actually bury, exactly where dense-sensor and CNN/POD methods fail. That removes the blocker (no dense sensors, no labeled per-kiln dataset) that has kept the interior temperature field unobservable.
parsed.feasibility_now: Not drop-in. The neuraloperator/RecFNO library is HIGH maturity, but this specific deployment is MEDIUM: it requires training data the user must generate -- either a finite-element/CFD pyrolysis simulation of the earth mound or a few fully instrumented reference kilns -- and the model risks out-of-distribution transfer across wood species, mound geometry, and moisture, so it needs domain-randomized simulation plus field calibration. Hardware is modest (a handful of high-temp thermocouples and a logger, no special camera), but expect real physics-modeling and validation engineering before the reconstructed field is trustworthy enough to drive harvest decisions.
parsed.primary_quote: The internal temperature FIELD is unobservable -- only a few surface points can be measured.

reasoning_trace.reasoning: The open problem is literally a field-reconstruction problem stated as 'the internal temperature field is unobservable from only a few surface points' -- a one-to-one match for FNO's ability to recover a full continuous field from 5-10 sparse sensors. The mature alternatives (dense thermocouple grids, interior imaging, CNN/POD) are blocked because a buried earth mound cannot be densely instrumented or imaged and artisanal kilns never yield a labeled dense training set; FNO's sparse-input, resolution-invariant, super-resolution reconstruction is precisely the capability that bypasses that. Feasibility is realistic-not-optimistic because the technique still needs a simulated-physics or instrumented-kiln training set and faces OOD transfer across wood/geometry/moisture -- so it is engineering, not drop-in.
reasoning_trace.decision: Use an FNO to reconstruct the full internal kiln temperature field from 5-10 buried thermocouples, turning subjective smoke-color watching into a quantitative pyrolysis-endpoint and vent-control signal to raise yield
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - the library is mature but this deployment requires user-generated training data and faces out-of-distribution transfer, per the MEDIUM deploy tier
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: no faithful kiln pyrolysis simulation can be built and no reference kilns can be instrumented (so there is no training data), or the buried probes alter/cannot survive the burn, or per-mound geometry/wood variability makes the trained operator fail to transfer to new kilns
